Text.Text: Untouchable Instinct. Learned. I heard it in your feet before you got here, lighter than any two people I've tracked. Go. Don't lose it to comfort.
Eleven steps back. West trail. You've been coming since before the ridge line. Loud, still. Instinct isn't in your feet yet. Come back when it is.

You stopped when I said stop. Good ear, or good luck. The den's adepts hunt in noise, six of them, driving beasts loud enough to hide their own footsteps. Go into the Grotto Apex Den on Dathomir. Put the six down. Bring back the Untouchable Instinct Grotto Track Slate they carry. It still smells like the den it was cut from.
Take the key. Old drain gate, west face of the den. Quiet hinge, if you're quiet opening it. Go.

Instinct is moving before the thought finishes. Not fast. Early. Your body already agreed with the ground before your head catches up. Adepts don't have it. They think, then move, then get hit in the gap between.

Every den animal leaves scent on stone it crosses enough times. The slate reads that scent, turns it into trail. Adepts carry it to hunt with. You'll carry it back to me, and it goes back to just remembering.
Six of them, together, loud. They overwhelm by numbers, not skill, too many places to watch at once. Watch the gaps between them. That's where the ground stays honest.
Six adepts. One slate. Still out there.
Quieter already. Show me the slate.
Good. It remembers the den again, not the noise. There's more under that ridge, if you want it.

The five specialists don't hunt loud. They wait. Long enough to make you think the den's gone empty, then close from every side at once. Go back into the Grotto Apex Den. Put the five down. Bring me the Untouchable Instinct Resonant Fang Charm off one of them.
Same gate. Deeper in this time. Walk slower than you think you need to.
Adepts push. Specialists surround. They've learned patience is a weapon too, the den taught them that much honestly, even if they use it wrong. Silence first. Then five directions at once.

Fang charm hums against a wrist when something's closing that you haven't placed yet. Old clan warning. Specialists wear it to know when their own circle's tightened enough to strike. You'll wear it a while, coming back. Listen to it.
You don't out-wait them. You move before the circle closes, not after. That's the instinct again, early, not fast. Wait for the strike and you've already lost the only window you had.
Five specialists, still circling something. Bring the charm when they're not.
You've gone quiet in a way I like. Let's see the charm.
Good. That's a real warning back in real hands. You're starting to hear the gaps before they close.

There's a warden past the specialists. Fast. Never where your strike lands, never where you expect the next one from either. One blade against that just tires chasing air. Bring two who read ground the way you're learning to, spread out, cut his angles down to none. Put him down. Bring me the Untouchable Instinct Cracked Apex Totem he carries.
Same gate. He'll hear you before you hear him. Bring your two in quiet, spread wide, close together only when you strike.
Trained him once. Fast even then. The den made him faster and took his patience in trade, now he only ever fights, never waits. That's not skill anymore. That's a man who forgot how to stand still.
Cracked apex totem marked the den's true alpha trail. He broke his on the day he stopped standing still for anything, including his own clan. Bring it back whole and the trail's honest again.

Because he's smoke. One blade chases smoke and never catches it, just wears out swinging at where it was. Three blades, spread wide, and smoke has nowhere left that isn't someone's reach. That's not about strength. It's about leaving him no gap fast enough to slip through.
The warden's still out there, still too fast for one. Bring your two.
All three of you standing, moving slow now instead of chasing. Let's see what he was carrying.
Whole. Readable again. First honest blow this den's taken in longer than I've tracked. The inner circle will have felt the ground shift.

Four left who taught him to run instead of stand, the inner circle. They hunt in a ring, always moving, always covering each other's gaps. Bring your two back in; four of them moving is worse than one warden standing still. Put all four down. Bring me the Untouchable Instinct Den-Mother's Fang Token they keep between them.
Same gate. They already know you're coming, the ring always knows. Move with your two like it's one animal, not three.

Moving without settling. Never let a strike land clean because you're never still long enough to be hit clean either. It's instinct turned inside out, moved before thought, but moved away from everything, never toward. Empty version of the real thing.

Every den had a den-mother once, first beast the clan ever bonded honest. Her fang token got split four ways so no ring could ever hold the whole truth of her. Whole again, it's proof the den remembers something older than what runs it now.

Scent-language, mostly, each one holds a piece of how the den used to talk to the animals in it before the ring taught them to just run. My own beast spoke that language once. I still recognize the shape of it in these, even broken.
The ring's still moving out there. Four of them. Bring the token back whole.
Still three of you, still standing. Let's see the token.
Whole. The ring's gone quiet for the first time since I started tracking it. One voice left, and it's the one that taught the ring to run in the first place. You're close now.

Last one. The master doesn't run like the ring and doesn't wait like the warden, he does both, faster than either, because he's the one who taught them the pieces. What you're chasing all this way, moving before thought, agreeing with the ground before your head catches up, he already has, whole. Bring your two. Alone, you're just another set of footsteps he heard coming long before you got here. Nothing to carry back for this one. Him going still is the proof.
Then go quiet, and go together. He'll hear one set of footsteps easy. Three, moving as one, he has to actually listen for.

The ring runs. The warden waits and strikes. He does both at once, and never stops doing either. That's the whole instinct, mastered and turned wrong: never still, never late, never where the ground says he should be. You've been building the same thing in yourself this whole trial. He's just further along it, and pointed the wrong way.

Because smoke that fast doesn't have a seam for one blade to find. Three, moving wide, moving together, and there's finally a moment he can't be everywhere at once. That moment is the whole fight. Miss it alone and you just get tired first.

Mine went still, once, at the wrong moment, against something faster than either of us. I've tracked every fast thing in this den since, trying to understand what I missed. I think I finally do. I just can't be the one who tests it.
He's still out there. Still too fast for one. Bring your two.
Quiet. The whole den's gone still, and it's never gone still in all the time I've tracked it. Tell me it's him.

Then it's done. Instinct the way it's supposed to run: early, not fast, agreeing with the ground before your head even asks it to. My own beast never got that far with me. Yours will. Go. Don't lose it to comfort, and don't come back here loud.
Back to the ground.
I'll take the six and bring the slate.
What is instinct, really?
What does the slate carry?
What am I listening for down there?
Not yet.
Here's the Untouchable Instinct Grotto Track Slate.
Back to the ground.
I'll take the five and bring the charm.
What's different about them?
What does the fang charm do?
How do I fight something that waits?
Give me a day.
Here's the Untouchable Instinct Resonant Fang Charm.
Back to the ground.
I'll bring two and take the warden.
Who is he?
What's the apex totem?
Why can't I just outlast him alone?
Not until I've got my two.
Here's the Untouchable Instinct Cracked Apex Totem, whole.
Back to the ground.
We'll take the ring, all three of us.
What do they actually teach?
What's the den-mother's fang token?
What carries in these tokens, really?
Company needs rest.
Here's the Untouchable Instinct Den-Mother's Fang Token, whole.
Back to the ground.
We're going in for the master.
What makes him different from the ring and the warden?
Why three, against something that fast?
What happened to your own beast?
Not until we're ready.
It's done. He's still.
